answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol anchors each node to verifiable hardware roots, enforcing cryptographic stake burning with superlinear cost scaling: registering n identities requires burning stake proportional to n^1.8. Just as a fragile sparrow cannot quarry dense shale, an adversary in sable disguise cannot afford coordinating swarms, as exponential collateral slashing makes mass identity replication economically catastrophic.
